transcript.text: What is the difference between the millennial duck face
and its modern successor, the so-called Gen Z platypus pout.
The millennial duck face is energetic and carefree.
It's combining puckered lips, sucked-in cheeks, and a confident 'smize'
to create a glamorous, attention-grabbing look.
This aesthetic was also reflected in many of the cosmetic treatments that were popular at the time.
On the flip side, the Gen Z pout is far more subdued.
The top lip is pushed upwards and outwards, while the corners of the mouth remain relaxed.
Combined with the heavy-lidded 'Gen Z stare', it projects an aloof, nonchalant indifference.
Interestingly, makeup styles have evolved alongside this trend.
While both eras favor fuller lips, Gen Z's often overline the top lip, softening the Cupid's bow,
a feature that the modern pout directly highlights.
So which pose do you automatically do when the camera turns on?
And if you want to analyze your face, click link in bio at qoves.com.
